variants.note: own massing_affinities: cross-gable-victorian canonical ('the intersecting gabled block is the workhorse form'), massed-picturesque canonical.

CASCADE-PROVENANCE FIX. Before this override the slot wrongly resolved to 'hip... kept behind a parapet, the roof is never the composed feature' from english-palladian -- flatly contradicted by this style's own defining_characteristics ('Steep roof pitches... prominent cross gables and dormers') and by massing_affinities, which forbids the symmetrical four-over-four box outright: 'contradicts the plan-driven asymmetry that defines the style after 1840.' A Palladian hip roof concealed behind a parapet is the opposite of everything this style is built to reject (Pugin's Contrasts, 1836).

roof_form.rule: Steeply pitched, intersecting cross-gables generated by the plan, never a hipped roof hidden behind a parapet. The silhouette is meant to be broken (defining_characteristics).

variants.note: own typical_ratios: '50-55 degrees typical in slate or plain tile.'

CASCADE-PROVENANCE FIX. Wrongly resolved to Mediterranean half-round barrel tile ('coppi e embrici') via mediterranean-vernacular -- a hot-dry-climate material with no place in Victorian Britain and no mention anywhere in this style's own text, which names slate and plain tile explicitly.

roof_material.rule: Slate or plain clay tile, laid to the style's own steep pitch (45-60 degrees).

variants.note: defining_characteristics #4: 'Structural expression as an ethical requirement: exposed roof timbers, visible lintels and relieving arches.' The eave is where the roof structure is meant to be seen, not concealed under a moulded cornice.

CASCADE-PROVENANCE FIX. Wrongly resolved from mediterranean-vernacular (paired brackets, 600-1200 mm projection) -- an Italianate villa device with no connection to this style's own ethic of visible timber construction.

eave_condition.rule: The eave exposes real roof structure -- rafter feet, purlins, sometimes a moulded barge board on the gable -- consistent with Pugin's principle that ornament may only enrich necessary construction.
eave_condition.note: EDITORIAL: eave detail specifically is not named verbatim in this node's own text; the correction is grounded in the style's explicit, repeatedly-stated structural-honesty ethic (defining_characteristics, description.long) rather than a direct quotation about the eave.

variants.note: diagnostic_tells: 'Banded structural polychromy -- courses of red and black brick or two stones alternating -- which is a High Victorian invention.' Hard co-occurrence constraint c03: 'Polychromy must be in the material... never painted or rendered on. This is the one rule High Victorian architects never broke.'
Also documented, particularly in the earlier and ecclesiastical/collegiate register (Palace of Westminster exemplar).

The plain single-colour Georgian brick this style's own trades descended from (real lineage, english-georgian, weight 0.7) remains structurally correct but is NOT the diagnostic High Victorian expression -- polychromy is what marks a building genuinely of this style after 1850.
Hard constraint c03: never painted or rendered.

primary_cladding.rule: Where the building is High Victorian (post-1850), polychromy must be structural -- different bricks or stones bonded into the wall, never applied as paint or render (hard constraint c03). Earlier and ecclesiastical work may be plain Georgian-descended brick or ashlar without banding.

variants.note: CASCADE-PROVENANCE FIX. Wrongly resolved from english-georgian ('modillion-cornice... a full classical entablature at the eaves') -- directly contradicted by this style's own hard constraint c05: 'Classical apparatus -- orders, pediments, entablatures, quoins, symmetrical porticoes -- is forbidden throughout.' A modillion cornice IS an entablature member.
Consistent with the style's own polychromy and exposed-construction ethic (c03, defining_characteristics).

cornice.rule: No classical entablature-derived cornice (hard constraint c05). Where the eave needs a finishing course, it is corbelled brick or a plain moulded stone course, in the same banded material logic as the wall.

parapet.rule: CASCADE-PROVENANCE FIX. Wrongly resolved from english-baroque as a 'balustraded' parapet 'concealing the roof... carrying urns, statuary.' This contradicts the style at two independent points: hard constraint c05 forbids classical apparatus (a balustrade is one), and the roof itself is never concealed -- it is the primary silhouette element the style is built around (defining_characteristics, diagnostic_tells).

variants.note: Hard constraint c01: 'Every arch is pointed and every pointed opening must be structurally plausible -- a real arch with voussoirs or a real relieving arch above a lintel.'
diagnostic_tells names 'pointed or square-headed stone openings' together; a square head is licensed provided it carries a label/drip mould (below).

CASCADE-PROVENANCE FIX. Wrongly resolved from english-baroque ('an oversized keystone') -- a keystone is classical apparatus, forbidden outright by hard constraint c05, and no genuine arch this style uses is a classical segmental-keyed arch.

window_head_masonry.rule: Every arched opening is genuinely pointed and structurally real -- 'applied pointed trim over a square opening is precisely what Pugin's True Principles forbids' (c01). Square-headed openings are licensed but never carry a classical keystone.

variants.note: defining_characteristics: 'Label or drip moulds over openings, buttresses where thrust actually occurs, and traceried, cusped or plate-traceried windows.'
CASCADE-PROVENANCE FIX. Wrongly resolved from english-palladian -- a licensed classical exotic opening with no place in a style whose c05 forbids classical apparatus throughout.

special_window.rule: The special window is Gothic tracery -- cusped, plate-traceried or grouped under a shared pointed label -- never a classical Venetian or Diocletian opening.

variants.note: diagnostic_tells: 'A steeply gabled asymmetrical front with a projecting buttressed porch.' Buttresses are licensed only where real thrust occurs (hard constraint c02).

CASCADE-PROVENANCE FIX. Wrongly resolved from english-georgian ('the entrance carries the order... Gibbs's plates') -- a fully classical Georgian device, the exact vocabulary c05 forbids throughout this style.

door_surround.rule: A projecting, gabled and buttressed porch with a pointed arch and hood mould -- never a classical pilaster-and-entablature doorcase (hard constraint c05).

transom_sidelight.rule: CASCADE-PROVENANCE FIX. Wrongly resolved from adam-style as a 'radiating fanlight... as delicate as the plasterwork inside' -- a refined late-Georgian neoclassical device that has no place under hard constraint c05's blanket prohibition on classical apparatus. Not directly named in this node's own text (hence editorial), but a semicircular fanlight is unambiguously the family of ornament c05 excludes.
transom_sidelight.note: EDITORIAL: not directly documented either way; forbidden on the strength of c05's general prohibition rather than a direct quotation about fanlights specifically.

variants.note: No historical precedent (docs/inheritance.md). Housed in a subordinate service wing or outbuilding gable, treated as one more plan-driven functional volume rather than a symmetrical attached bay -- consistent with the style's own plan-first, asymmetrical logic.

garage_strategy.rule: INVENTED, no historical precedent. A subordinate gabled service volume, generated by the plan like any other room -- never a centred, symmetrical attached bay.

pediment.rule: CASCADE-PROVENANCE FIX. british-picturesque deliberately left this slot OPEN at the family level because two of its three members (Queen Anne, Baronial) use a pediment as applied ornament -- but that family-level judgment does not apply to THIS member. gothic-revival-british's own hard constraint c05 explicitly names 'pediments' among the classical apparatus 'forbidden throughout.' Left open at the family kit, the cascade instead ran past it to english-palladian and produced a fully-worked classical pediment rule, which is exactly what c05 rules out for this node. Overridden here on the affected node's own kit, per docs/inheritance.md's cascade-bug guidance.

pilaster.rule: Same cascade-provenance fix as `pediment`. Hard constraint c05 names 'orders' among the forbidden classical apparatus, and a pilaster is a flattened order; this style's own text never uses one.

balustrade.rule: Same cascade-provenance fix as `pediment`. Hard constraint c05's prohibition and the absence of any balustrade in this style's own defining_characteristics or diagnostic_tells (which instead name buttresses, label moulds, gables and tracery) both point the same way.

ornament_vocabulary.rule: Same cascade-provenance fix as `pediment`, corrected to the style's own actual vocabulary rather than left to leak a classical Palladian rule: structural polychromy, label and drip moulds, cusped and plate tracery, foliate and naturalistic carving confined to real structural members -- ornament is enrichment of necessary construction, never applied decoration (defining_characteristics, description.long).

principal_storey_height.note: SOURCE UNIT NOTE: this node's own typical_ratios give 3.3-4.3 m at principal level; recorded here as metres, not the ft this parameter's unit enum lists, because no ft-denominated figure is stated -- treat the numeric value as metres despite the unit field (schema limitation, no 'm' unit exists).

graduation.note: Storeys are generally UNIFORM rather than graduated -- own typical_ratios: 'the loss of Georgian graduation is itself a diagnostic.'

ceiling_height_rule.rule: CASCADE-PROVENANCE FIX. Wrongly resolved as an extends from renaissance-classical/english-palladian's Palladian arithmetic/geometric/harmonic-mean room derivation, checkable 'against a published plate' -- flatly incompatible with this style's own stated method: 'No applied system. Proportion is derived from medieval precedent by measurement... composition is picturesque.' Corrected: ceiling height follows the room's function within the plan, not a mean-of-plan-dimensions formula, and storeys are deliberately NOT graduated the way Georgian ones are.

variants.note: description.long: rooms carry exposed roof timbers, encaustic tile, stained glass and structural expression carried indoors; defining_characteristics #4 ('ornament confined to the enrichment of real structural members') applies as much to interior trim as to the exterior.

CASCADE-PROVENANCE FIX. Wrongly resolved from english-georgian -- a fully classical Georgian profile family, incompatible with c05's blanket prohibition and with this style's own structural-honesty ethic.

trim_family.rule: Interior trim follows the same structural-honesty ethic as the exterior: exposed timber, pointed-arch panelling and enrichment confined to real structural members, never a classical Georgian moulding family.
trim_family.note: EDITORIAL for the specific profile vocabulary (not itemized in this node's own text at the level of baseboard/casing dimensions), grounded directly in the style's repeatedly-stated structural-honesty principle.

variants.note: defining_characteristics: 'the plan drawn first, the facade a consequence.' Own massing_affinities: h-plan-manor common, 'where the client wanted a great hall and the architect obliged with a screens passage -- Scott and Pugin both did this repeatedly.'

CASCADE-PROVENANCE FIX. Wrongly resolved from english-classical, which explicitly forbids the very 'cross-passage' parti this style's own massing_affinities documents as common practice ('the medieval and vernacular partis... never appear here' -- a rule about the CLASSICAL family that is being wrongly applied to a style built specifically to reject it).

circulation_parti.rule: Circulation follows the plan, not a fixed classical hall-and-stair figure: a great hall and screens passage where the programme calls for one (h-plan-manor), otherwise an asymmetrical arrangement generated by room function.

variants.note: description.long: 'The rooms are tall and the windows are large but the glass is often coloured, so the light arrives tinted and heavy.'

CASCADE-PROVENANCE FIX. Wrongly resolved from mediterranean-vernacular's 5-20% aperture-to-wall figure -- a hot-dry-climate thermal-mass strategy directly contradicted by this style's own text, which describes large windows and abundant (if tinted) glazing.

daylight_strategy.rule: Windows are large; daylighting is generous even where the glass itself is coloured or leaded, which changes the quality of light without reducing the aperture.
daylight_strategy.note: EDITORIAL: this node's own text gives no aperture-percentage figure, so the correction removes the wrong borrowed number rather than asserting a false precise one.
